item.title: OpenAI Gave Me Six Months of ChatGPT Pro for Maintaining Open Source
item.author: blog@baifan.site (ByF (BaiFan))
item.description:
An email popped up in my inbox today: “You can just build things, enjoy 6 months on us.”

Sender: the Codex team at OpenAI. The first line, in big letters: “You’re in.” Then: “Thanks for maintaining open source projects.”

I stared at that line three times and couldn’t help laughing out loud.

A while back I filled out their Codex for Open Source application on a whim. Didn’t expect much — I just listed the PRs I’d submitted to context-mode, plus my own byf and dev-skills.

item.title: AI API Suffixes: What They Mean and Why They Exist
item.author: blog@baifan.site (ByF (BaiFan))
item.description:
We often see URLs like these:

1
2
3

/v1/chat/completions
/v1/messages
/v1/responses

These suffixes are not decoration — they define a complete request and response data structure. Pick the wrong one and your code either errors out or silently loses data.

This article starts at /v1/completions and works its way to /v1/responses, explaining what each suffix stands for, why it was designed that way, and where the common pitfalls are.
